 Game Notes Box Score (PDF) Florida lost for the first time this season, falling 86-76 against eighth-ranked Houston. Cougars Take It to Gators Inside
 Wednesday, November 18, 2026 | Men's Basketball, Chris Harry
 Box Score Share: By: Chris Harry, Senior Writer 
 LAS VEGAS  – So much of the identity of the Florida basketball program under Todd Golden , especially with the current nucleus of veteran players, has been wrapped in what the Gators do around the basket in wearing opponents down over 40 minutes with physicality and relentless energy in the paint. 
The fact that Houston did those things better Wednesday in handing the No. 1 Gators their first loss of the season wasn't that big a surprise. Similar traits have been the calling card of Kelvin Sampson's teams for years. 
No, the surprise was in just how badly the eighth-ranked Cougars dominated the Gators in virtually every power category on the way to an 86-76 upset in second-round play of the Players Era 8 at Michelob ULTRA Arena. 
UH senior guard Dedan Thomas Jr. poured in a career-high 30 points to lead the Cougars (5-0), but his numbers – and they were impressive – only told part of the story. Thomas riddled the UF defense with penetrating probes and pull-ups, hitting 10 of his 17 field-goal attempts (and needing only two 3-point tries, both of which he made) and all eight free throws without a committing a turnover. 
Thomas proved the main culprit in a Houston offense that outscored UF 44-18 in the paint, out-rebounded the Gators overall 32-26, but also 13-9 on the offensive end on the way to 16 second-chance points. The Cougars shot 62.1% in the second half and attempted just one 3-point along the way. They didn't need any long ones. They were getting all the short ones they wanted.
 Houston guard Dedan Thomas (9) drove and dropped shots on the Gators' defense all game on his way to 30 points.
Photo by USA Today 
"I'm surprised we did such a poor job defending the paint, which is something we're usually really good at," Golden said after the much-hyped rematch of the 2025 NCAA championship game that his team won in a 65-63 rock fight. "Credit to Houston. They did a really good job up in there."
And they got to the free-throw line 27 times, converting 25 of them (92.6%), while Florida attempted only nine free throws. The UF coach was surprised at that, too. 
"I thought it was a very physical game. I thought both teams were very physical," he said. "There are games you're going to lose the free-throw battle, but when they shoot 27 and you shoot nine when you're attacking and trying to get into the paint as well, that's a little frustrating."
Probably more so considering the Gators bombed in 15 3-pointers, their most in 75 games dating to early in their '24-25 title season, on 26 attempts. Guard Denzel Aberdeen made six of them on his way to a career-high 26 points, with forward Thomas Haugh adding 18 points on a quarter of 3s. Backup guard Urban Klavzar made all of his from distance on his way to 14 points.
Yet, they played from behind virtually the entire second half and never mounted much of a threat. The loss dropped the the Gators (5-1) into the tournament's consolation bracket, where they'll face West Virginia (4-1), an 86-82 loser to 11 th -ranked Kansas, in the event's third-place game Thursday at 2:30 p.m. 
"We just have to guard better," Aberdeen said. 
And rebound better. The Cougars, who trailed 40-37 at halftime, got back 65% of their misses in the second half, went 12-for-12 at the free-throw line and led by as many 14 points in outscoring the Gators 49-36 after the break.
"We're not going to outshoot anyone. We're not that kind of team," Sampson said. "But we can own the paint." 
 Three Cougars converge on Thomas Haugh (center), who still managed to score 18 points and hit four 3-pointers. 
They owned it by limiting the production of UF stalwarts Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu , who combined for just 12 points and 12 rebounds, plus five turnovers in their 63 minutes. 
Houston forward Joseph Tugler had 12 points and 10 rebounds, with sidekick Delrecco Gillespie adding eight points and eight rebounds. Florida actually had more problems with the Cougars' guard trio of Thomas, Chase McCarty and backup Chendall Weaver, who combined for 52 points on 18-for-30 shooting (and just three 3-pointers), even with UF starting point man and best perimeter defender Boogie Fland playing 30 minutes through a sore shoulder that him questionable heading into the game.
"Their guards got us," Golden said. 
UF shot 51.9% and hit nine 3s in the first half, but led by only three at intermission, 40-37, by turning the ball over seven times and sending UH to the free-throw line 15 times. 
 DENZEL ABERDEEN FROM HALF COURT 🤯🤯 https://t.co/3dzsBivX56
— The Field of 68 (@TheFieldOf68) November 18, 2026 
The Gators' lead was gone early in the second, with the Cougars scoring the first six points. UF retook the lead twice, but Houston ripped off a run of 11 consecutive points, all in the paint, with the first two buckets by Thomas, followed an old-time 3-point play from Miller, to roll ahead to a 57-47 advantage. 
Twice the Gators got within four after that, but the second time was answered by three straight buckets (all in the paint) by McCarty for another 10-point cushion that was never threatened. 
"Disappointing result for us today," Golden said. "I told the team before the game if we could win the turnover battle and rebounding battle we'd be in good shape."
UH was a combined plus-12 in those two categories and won by 10 points. 
Now, comes a brutally quick turn-around – about 20 hours for the Gators, just 17 for the Mountaineers – and, if it's any consolation, a second Quadrant 1 opportunity against a solid West Virginia team in a third-game-in-three-days consolation match-up.
Both teams figure to be exhausted. 
The one that came to the desert with the big orange-and-blue No. 1 target on its back will need to play better, tougher and with more physicality down low. Like it usually does.
